images.title: How fast do animals move
images.purpose: Show the infographic of top speeds of 15 animals in air, on land and in water that the questions refer to.
images.composition: Fifteen vertical bars in three colour groups with an animal silhouette under each, a speed scale up the side, a legend at the top.
exact_structure: A vertical scale from 0 to 322 kph with labels at 0, 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 129, 145, 161, 177, 193, 209, 225, 241, 257, 274, 290, 306 and 322, with faint gridlines.

Five light blue bars for speed in air, each with its speed printed inside the top: peregrine falcon 322 kph, spine tailed swift 170 kph, free tailed bat 96 kph, green darner dragonfly 64 kph, flying fish 56 kph.
Five brick red bars for speed on land: cheetah 103 kph, pronghorn antelope 88 kph, ostrich 64 kph, human 37 kph, Australian tiger beetle 8 kph.
Five dark blue bars for speed in water: sailfish 109 kph, dolphin 40 kph, California sea lion 40 kph, Gentoo penguin 35 kph, humpback whale 26 kph.
Each bar has a small flat silhouette of its animal and its name below it.
A legend at the top: light blue labelled speed in air, brick red labelled speed on land, dark blue labelled speed in water.
rejection: bars in a different order or colour group
images.takeaway: The bars are bars of a bar graph, but the scale labels go up in uneven steps of about 16 kph.
images.description: An infographic bar chart of the top speeds of fifteen animals in air, on land and in water.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point out the uneven scale labels (112 to 129 is 17) before students answer the scale question.

images.title: Electric vehicles registered per year
images.purpose: Show the clustered bar graph of electric vehicle registrations with empty rows for Gujarat and Delhi that students complete.
images.composition: A horizontal clustered bar graph: states down the left, registrations along the bottom, a legend at the top.
exact_structure: A horizontal axis from 0 to 100000 with numbered vertical guidelines at 0, 25000, 50000, 75000 and 100000, and lighter unnumbered guidelines halfway between them.
Seven state rows from top to bottom: Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam, Gujarat, Delhi.
Each of the first five rows has three bars: teal (#0072B2) for 2022, vermilion (#D55E00) for 2023, amber (#E69F00) for 2024.
Uttarakhand: about 15500, 16500 and 19000.
West Bengal: about 10500, 21500 and 43000.
Andhra Pradesh: about 29500, 34500 and 55000.
Odisha: about 27500, 44000 and 62500.
Assam: about 40000, 60000 and 64500.
The Gujarat and Delhi rows have three empty outlined bar slots each, with no bars filled in.
No values are printed on the bars.
labels: Number of electric vehicles registered per year
rejection: any bar drawn for Gujarat or Delhi
a scale not in steps of 25000
images.takeaway: Bars are read against the guidelines, so a small change in length can still be thousands of vehicles.
images.description: A clustered bar graph of electric vehicle registrations in seven states for 2022, 2023 and 2024, with Gujarat and Delhi left blank.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students draw the Gujarat and Delhi bars themselves; the top of each bar only needs to fall between the right guidelines.

images.title: Pick a scale that fits
images.purpose: Show how to choose a scale: the largest value decides how high the vertical line must go.
images.composition: A simple bar graph with two bars in the centre, plenty of white space around it, and one scale note to the right.
exact_structure: One vertical axis with exactly 5 evenly spaced marks labelled 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 from bottom to top, and one horizontal baseline.
Two upright bars of equal width standing on the baseline: a teal #0072B2 bar reaching 38 and an amber #E69F00 bar reaching 25, drawn to that scale.
The value 38 is written just above the teal bar and 25 just above the amber bar.
The top of the teal bar is close below the 40 mark, with a thin reddish purple #CC79A7 dashed line from the top of the teal bar to the 40 mark.
To the right of the graph, one short note: 1 step = 10.
rejection: a bar height that does not match its value on the scale
images.takeaway: Look at the largest value first, then pick equal steps so it fits on the axis.
images.description: A two-bar graph with bars of 38 and 25 on an axis marked 0 to 40 in steps of 10.
images.context: Shown on the practice concept before the scale-choosing questions.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the axis stops at 40 and not at 30 or 100.

image_decisions.why: Two questions are read from figures: the animal speed infographic and the electric vehicle graph.
